addressed_note: Tags no longer overlap/clip in live screenshot media/s11_a.png; leader lines and speech-bubble stacking queued as todos; dashboard text wrap done (#32); restart claim withdrawn.
summary: The stacking helps in the author's close-up shot, but in the live game now Hopscotch/Sprout still overlap and Cumulus is cut off at the bottom edge, so #29 is not fully done. The 'verified live, no restart' claim for #31 is weak: the game restarted repeatedly this session.

findings.what: Name tags still overlap in the live game. Hopscotch and Sprout are drawn on top of each other. Cumulus is cut off by the bottom edge of the viewport, so the 'clamped to viewport' claim does not hold vertically.
findings.where: scenery.jl:263-282 stack_offsets (only x is clamped in clamp_dx; y is never clamped to the viewport). Screen area: bottom left of the 3D view.
findings.evidence: world/reviews/s10_review.png (live_screenshot taken during review). Compare world/media/s10_b.png, which shows a clean case.
findings.suggestion: Clamp y into [margin, height-margin] after stacking. Stack upward from the lowest label and fall back to stacking downward when the top is reached. Test with the creatures piled at the bottom of the frame.

findings.what: The evidence is one hand-picked camera angle where the four creatures sit under one tree. s10_b.png is a fresh process (clock 00:00, versus 23:30 in s10_a.png), so the before/after pair compares two different game runs, not a Revise reload of the same state. The claim that Revise applied the edit without a restart is not supported.
findings.evidence: Clock 23:30 vs 00:00; panel text in s10_a says 'game exited with code 0 after 763.3 s'. events-2026-11-22.jsonl has game_start at 17:03:07 and 17:07:04 (16 starts today); the review screenshot shows 'game exited with code 0 after 228.3 s'.
findings.suggestion: Find out why the game keeps exiting with code 0 every few minutes. Verify #31 by showing the same process (same frame counter) before and after the edit.

findings.what: Labels are stacked far above the creatures and sit on the tree canopy. In s10_b the four tags float well above the animals, with no leader line or marker, so it is unclear which tag belongs to which creature. Only 4 of 10 creatures are tagged in that view.
findings.where: scenery.jl:293-296 (base offset 16, then pushed up by 1.15*fs per collision)
findings.suggestion: Cap the push distance and nudge sideways first. Draw a thin line to the head, or fade the tags that are pushed far.

findings.what: Performance is fine in steady state (frame median 1.1 ms, panels 1.2 ms, sync 1.0 ms). Just after a restart, though, frame p95 was 18.7 s: sync took 18.6 s, which is compile time. stack_offsets runs project() for every creature every frame and allocates arrays; this is cheap now but is O(n^2).
findings.evidence: live_status after restart: frame p95 18757 ms, median 1.1 ms
findings.suggestion: Accept for 10 creatures. Consider a warm-up call at startup so the first frames are not slow.

findings.what: The dashboard panel text is still truncated with ellipses, and the speech bubbles do not use the stacking. The author listed both as next steps.
findings.suggestion: Reuse stack_offsets for the speech bubbles.
